Controller Area Network (CAN) Protocol Specification 1.  Overview
The Controller Area Network (CAN) is an ISO standard (ISO 11898) for serial communications.  It was originally developed by Robert Bosch GmbH in 1986 for automotive applications.  CAN is designed to allow microcontrollers and devices to communicate with each other in applications without a host computer.
2.  Physical Layer
The CAN physical layer uses differential signaling via two wires: CAN High (CAN_H) and CAN Low (CAN_L).

In the recessive state, both lines are driven to 2.5V. 

In the dominant state, CAN_H goes to 3.5V and CAN_L drop.
